title: Sell Mineral Rights in Palermo, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Palermo, ND
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Palermo, ND in the Bakken core? Mountrail County acreage here has real production history. Get a fair, honest offer.
heroLead: Palermo is a small unincorporated community, but the Mountrail County ground around it sits well within the productive core of the Bakken, which surprises some families who assume value tracks town size.
intro: The mineral rights owned by Palermo-area families are usually tied to the same original homestead patents that most of central Mountrail County was settled under, and after the Parshall discovery well in 2006, this whole stretch of the county saw a wave of leasing and drilling. A lot of that acreage is still producing today, just further along the decline curve than it was in the boom years.

sections.heading: Core Bakken acreage, mature production
paragraphs: Wells drilled near Palermo in the years after the initial Bakken discovery are mostly past their peak now, which is normal and doesn't mean the interest has lost all its value, just that a fair offer reflects current decline rather than boom-era production. We look at your specific well's recent history before naming a number.

sections.heading: Confirming your ownership share
paragraphs: Because this ground has often been divided among several heirs since the original owner, we confirm your exact decimal interest through the Mountrail County Recorder before making an offer, so you know precisely what fraction of the well you're being paid for.

sections.heading: What Palermo-area statements tend to show
paragraphs: Owners here often have a good decade or more of royalty history to look at, which gives us a clear picture of how a specific well has declined over time. Some tracts have seen a second wave of infill drilling that bumped production back up temporarily before settling into a steadier long-term rate.
We look at that full production history, not only the most recent statement, because a well's trajectory tells us more about fair value than any single month's check does.

faqs.question: Our well near Palermo was drilled back in 2008. Is it still worth anything?
faqs.answer: Often yes, even mature wells continue producing at a lower, steadier rate for years, and that continued production still has value to a buyer.

faqs.question: How do we find out our exact ownership percentage?
faqs.answer: Send us your Division Order or a recent statement and we'll confirm your decimal interest against the Mountrail County recorder's records.

faqs.question: Can we sell even though the well is in decline?
faqs.answer: Yes, decline is factored into how we value the interest, not a reason we won't make an offer.

faqs.question: Was there a second wave of drilling near Palermo after the initial boom?
faqs.answer: In some spacing units, yes, infill wells targeting the Three Forks bench came later and boosted production again. We check whether that applies to your specific tract.
